children: Democratic lawmakers have expanded their investigation into alleged conflicts of interest within the Trump administration, focusing on companies associated with Donald Trump Jr that they allege may have improperly benefited from government contracts or regulatory concessions, according to multiple media reports on Tuesday.
Jamie Raskin — who is expected to lead the House judiciary committee in January — on Monday sought records from gambling platform Polymarket
Polymarket, Hadrian and Juul are backed by 1789 Capital, which Trump Jr joined as a partner soon after his father won the 2024 election, while GrabAGun was separately backed by the president’s son.

“1789 Capital has become remarkably adept at ‘timing’ its investments in companies shortly before they benefited from lucrative federal contracts and favourable regulatory actions,” Raskin wrote to the four groups in letters seen by the
, demanding they preserve all communications with the group.

GrabAGun said: “Congressman Raskin’s letter is a political document, and its allegations are baseless.” Bill Burck, a lawyer representing 1789 Capital, said: “We responded to Congressman Raskin back in September, pointing out in detail the many flaws in his understanding of how 1789 has operated and a number of basic factual errors. He never bothered to reply.”
Raskin and presumed incoming oversight committee chair Robert Garcia have vowed to go after the Trump family’s businesses when they take control of Congress next year.

In his letters, Raskin alleged that GrabAGun, Polymarket and Juul benefited from regulatory changes enacted by the Trump administration after the companies had secured investments from 1789. Hadrian received a nearly $1B US government contract in March, months after 1789 made its first investment. Raskin wrote that 1789’s record “suggests that either Donald Trump Jr suddenly acquired and brought to 1789 Capital magical new clairvoyant powers . . . or we are witnessing a brazen conspiracy to use the machinery of the executive branch of government under the control of President Trump to rig both public policy and the markets in order to enrich the first family”.

The FT reported that Hadrian chief executive Chris Power in July donated almost $450,000 to Republican causes just months after the company won a $900M contract from the US government. 1789 Capital upped its stake in the defence group in a fundraising round in August. At the time, 1789 said that “any statement or suggestion, directly or indirectly, that 1789 has a conflict-of-interest, or that it is somehow participating in or benefiting from any form of corruption, is provably false and defamatory”.

Hadrian said it was “proud to have the support of a broad and diverse group of investors” . . . “their support reflects broad confidence in Hadrian’s mission and our ability to deliver the manufacturing capacity America needs”. Polymarket and its rival Kalshi
gained popularity in the run-up to the 2024 election and attract billions of dollars in trading volume each month.

title: Democrats probe Polymarket, GrabAGun, Juul and Hadrian over links to Donald Trump Jr.
